stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs lose $635 million in a day, the biggest outflow since June
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs, funds that hold bitcoin for stock-market investors, saw about $635 million leave on Thursday, according to SoSoValue data reported by crypto.news. That wipes out more than half of the roughly $1.08 billion that came in over the three days before.
points: Net outflow of $635.49M on Thursday 22 Oct, the largest single day since June 25, per SoSoValue via crypto.news.
It ended a three-day inflow run of about $1.08B; October flows are now about $174.5M negative, per crypto.news.
By fund: BlackRock's IBIT -$254.05M, Fidelity's FBTC -$217.46M, ARK's ARKB -$109.43M, Grayscale's GBTC -$29.53M; only MSBT took in money (+$2.33M), per TokenPost citing SoSoValue.
Crypto Briefing also reports a $635M outflow, with IBIT down $254M.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $81,500 after Thursday's tech-stock sell-off
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell with tech stocks on Thursday, when the Nasdaq had its worst day since June, and has been trading between about $81,000 and $82,000 since. Traders are watching whether $80,000 holds, per The Block. Right now bitcoin is moving like a risky tech stock, so stock-market swings matter for crypto too.
points: Bitcoin was at $81,449.88 on 23 Oct, down 0.97%, after an intraday low near $80,989, per crypto.news (read about 07:15 UTC).
The Nasdaq fell 2.60% on Thursday to 26,008.86, its biggest one-day drop since June, led by chip stocks, per KuCoin's daily report.
Forced closures of leveraged bets: about $435M in 24 hours, $385M of them bets on a rise, per CoinDesk; The Block, citing CoinGlass, puts it at $440.9M.
Laevitas told The Block bitcoin is "trading as a high-beta tech position", meaning it swings more than stocks in both directions.

stories.title: Washington: a Senate probe into Tether payments, and crypto rules shifting to agencies
stories.summary: Sen. Richard Blumenthal, the top Democrat on the Senate's Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, wrote to Tether and to Nxum Group, a firm tied to former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines, about consulting payments. These are questions, not findings; Tether says an internal review found no wrongdoing. Separately, JPMorgan expects the CLARITY Act market-structure bill to stall this year, leaving US crypto rules to agencies.
points: The letter cites reporting that over $6M went from Tether to Nxum, under a May 2025 deal paying $415,000 a month, and asks for records by Nov 3, per the Senate letter.
Bo Hines now runs Tether's US business; Tether said outside counsel "found no evidence of wrongdoing", per CoinDesk.
JPMorgan expects the CLARITY Act to stall this year and possibly return in 2027, per The Block.
JPMorgan warns the current agency actions could be overturned "in as soon as two years, if a Democrat wins the White House", per The Block.
